cases.name: Tayanah "Tayou" Shelcy Edwidge Jean Paul
cases.about: Subsequent to the tragic earthquake in Haiti, Tayanah moved to the U.S.  As she grew up, she fell in love with dancing and singing. She was also extremely smart and adorable. She was very close to her family and friends; She smiled often and loved everyone and everything around her. Between us, our relationship was more than father/daughter and we spoke every day. We did our homework together daily. Tayanah was also my English teacher. I remember, one day, I mispronounced a word, she promptly corrected me and asked me to repeat the word again. Unfortunately, I still pronounced it wrongly to this day. Tayou said to me, ‘wouyyy Daddy, tet ou di”.  Two days before she passed away, we spent 1:37minutes on the phone discussing her dreams and aspirations, being a great dancer, singer, a great nurse or a great Doctor/Physician; when I asked why she would like to be one of those professionals, she answered “Dad, too many people are suffering, so I would like to have an opportunity to help and make a small contribution”.

cases.name: Nancy Lee Bogard Simmons
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "From an early age, Nancy radiated a remarkable confidence that left a lasting impression on everyone she met. Her spirited nature carried her gracefully throughout childhood and into young adulthood, shaping the strong, compassionate woman she became. In 1973, Nancy made her home in Orlando, where she built a beautiful life centered around family, friendship, and countless cherished memories.

A devoted mother, grandmother, great-grandmother and friend, Nancy found her greatest happiness in the time spent with those she held dear. Nancy's legacy is one of kindness, generosity, and unwavering devotion to her family. Her memory will forever be treasured by all who had the profound privilege of knowing and loving her. Though she will be deeply missed, the joy she shared so freely will continue to shine in the hearts of those she leaves behind."
cases.narrative: He allegedly shot her during an argument about going on a cruise. He claimed she was cursing at him, and he allegedly told her he had had enough and could pull the trigger. When she continued to curse at him, he allegedly pointed a shotgun at her and fired.
